name: Butthole Surfers
label: Touch and Go
lede: Trinity University's Accountant of the Year and an MBA student bought stolen strobe lights, hired a naked dancer, made the most deranged records of the eighties, then sued their own label and won.

eras.title: The accountant quits
eras.text: Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary were headed for business careers when a fake medical magazine derailed them. They went through a different band name every show until an emcee picked one for them, and a Dead Kennedys fan letter turned into a record deal.

years.src: Wikipedia · Our Band Could Be Your Life
years.h: Gibby Haynes gets caught with Strange V.D. at the office
years.p: Gibby Haynes, Trinity University basketball captain and Accountant of the Year, and MBA student Paul Leary make Strange V.D., a magazine of medical photos with invented captions. Haynes is caught with one at his accounting firm and leaves.
years.xp: Haynes moved to Southern California and Leary, one semester short of his degree, followed. They sold homemade clothing printed with Lee Harvey Oswald's face before heading back to San Antonio to start a band.

years.h: An emcee names the Butthole Surfers after one of their songs
years.p: Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary debut at the Bonham Exchange in San Antonio. At their first paid show, an emcee forgets the band's name and announces them by the title of their song Butthole Surfer, and it sticks.
years.xp:
Before that they used a new name every show. Haynes lists the Dick Clark Five, the Vodka Family Winstons, the Ashtray Babyheads and Ed Asner Is Gay among them.

Clubs, newspapers and radio stations spent the next two decades refusing to print or say the real name, calling them B.H. Surfers instead.

years.h: Jello Biafra sees the Butthole Surfers in San Francisco
years.p: The band moves to California in a van. [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] of [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] catches a short set at San Francisco's Tool and Die and offers to put out a record on Alternative Tentacles if they can book the studio time.

years.h: A fight ends the Mathews brothers' run; King Coffey arrives
years.p: Bassist Quinn Mathews and drummer Scott Mathews quit after a physical fight between Scott Mathews and Gibby Haynes. [[King Coffey|f275d56b-3601-476f-a4bf-b50892750984]] becomes the band's permanent drummer.

years.h: Butthole Surfers EP, a.k.a. Pee Pee the Sailor · Alternative Tentacles
years.p: Recorded at BOSS Studios in San Antonio, with The Shah Sleeps in Lee Harvey's Grave and Bar-B-Q Pope. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] listed it in his journals among his ten favorite albums.
play: The Shah Sleeps in Lee Harvey's Grave

years.h: Teresa Nervosa makes it two drummers
years.p: [[Teresa Taylor|4e998ae8-008c-4e85-8415-7903e9c4e265]], as Teresa Nervosa, joins as a second drummer. She and King Coffey play in unison on stand-up kits and were billed as siblings, though they weren't related.

eras.title: Stolen strobes and a studio hostage
eras.text: A studio owner held their first album hostage, so Alternative Tentacles put out a live record instead and Touch and Go got the album. On the road, the Butthole Surfers became the show people warned each other about.

years.h: Live PCPPEP fills in while Bob O'Neill holds the tapes
years.p: Studio owner Bob O'Neill won't release the Butthole Surfers' 1984 BOSS Studios masters until he's paid, and Alternative Tentacles can't pay. The label releases the live EP Live PCPPEP instead.

years.h: Psychic... Powerless... Another Man's Sac · Touch and Go
years.p: The Butthole Surfers' first album comes out on Touch and Go after booking agent Terry Tolkin brings them to [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]]. The song Butthole Surfer, source of the band's name, is on it.

years.src: Wikipedia · Our Band Could Be Your Life
years.h: Butthole Surfers buy thousands of dollars of stolen strobe lights
years.p: The band buys what was reported as several thousand dollars' worth of stolen strobes at a bargain. Soon the lights take up more room than the instruments.
years.xp:
They projected films behind them, often upside down or backwards: car crashes, nuclear blasts, meat processing and penis reconstruction surgery, plus a color negative of a Charlie's Angels episode. The strobes and films occasionally gave audience members seizures.

Gibby Haynes wore hundreds of clothespins, stripped down as the show went on, burst condoms full of stage blood and set a cymbal full of lighter fluid on fire, sometimes along with his hand.

years.h: Four bass players in a year, ending with Kramer
years.p: Terence Smart quits after falling in love; Canadian Trevor Malcolm quits in mid-1985; Juan Molina fills in for one tour. Before Europe, the Butthole Surfers call [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] of Shockabilly, who says yes.

years.h: Teresa Nervosa quits after a European tour
years.p: Worn out by touring, Teresa Nervosa leaves after a Christmas 1985 European tour. Drummer Kytha Gernatt, known as Cabbage, fills in. Touch and Go releases the Cream Corn from the Socket of Davis EP.

eras.title: A naked dancer and a burning cymbal
eras.text: The classic line-up came together in 1986, living in Georgia and then on a ranch outside Austin. These were the band's wildest shows and the three Touch and Go albums fans rank highest.

years.h: Rembrandt Pussyhorse, the album Alternative Tentacles passed on
years.p: Alternative Tentacles sat on the record for about a year, then turned it down. Touch and Go released a re-recorded version with a minimal rework of the Guess Who's American Woman.

years.h: Jeff Pinkus joins; Teresa Nervosa comes back
years.p: [[Jeff Pinkus|e72f5512-49b1-498f-98ff-26e3e39322aa]] replaces Kramer on bass and holds the job until 1994. Teresa Nervosa returns and Cabbage is fired, completing the classic Butthole Surfers line-up.

years.h: Kathleen Lynch becomes the Butthole Surfers' naked dancer
years.p: The band meets Kathleen Lynch, working at a New York strip club called Sex World. She is never an official member but dances with them, naked, through 1989.
years.xp: At a Washington, D.C. show with [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]] she danced in nothing but gold body paint and antique wooden snowshoes. She went by the name Ta-Da the Shit Lady.

years.src: Wikipedia · Our Band Could Be Your Life
years.h: The Butthole Surfers show that ended in fire and a screwdriver
years.p: At one 1986 show, Gibby Haynes starts a small fire after five songs, while Paul Leary attacks the club's speakers with a screwdriver.
years.xp: According to Michael Azerrad's Our Band Could Be Your Life, as summarized by Wikipedia, Haynes and Kathleen Lynch, both shaved bald by then, reportedly had sex onstage that night.

years.h: Locust Abortion Technician · Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded on cheap gear in a rented house in Winterville, Georgia. It opens with Sweat Loaf, a warped take on Black Sabbath's Sweet Leaf, under Arthur Sarnoff's painting of two clowns and a dog.
years.xp: Leary said the bad equipment forced them to be more creative. Kurt Cobain put it in his top 50 albums, and it reached No. 3 on the UK indie chart. Around its release the band bought a ranch house on five acres in Driftwood, Texas, about 30 miles from Austin, and turned it into a studio.

years.h: Hairway to Steven: no song titles, just cartoons
years.p: Cut in a week in January 1988 at January Sound in Dallas. The title spoonerizes Led Zeppelin's Stairway to Heaven, and each song is labeled with a crude cartoon instead of a name.
years.xp: Fans later matched the songs to titles using the 1989 Double Live album. It was Teresa Nervosa's last studio album with the band. Jeff Pinkus later said the faster, tidier sessions stifled some of their spontaneity.

years.h: Bar-B-Que Movie spoofs The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
years.p: Tom Stern and [[Alex Winter|28e5288b-1c6e-4b89-961c-287d5868ced9]] of Bill & Ted shoot a Super 8 short that ends with the Butthole Surfers, Kathleen Lynch, burning cymbal and all, playing the song Fast.

years.h: Double Live, the Butthole Surfers' answer to bootleggers
years.p: Recorded on a portable DAT on the winter 1988 tour, Double Live is the first release on the band's own Latino Buggerveil label.

years.h: Teresa Nervosa leaves; an aneurysm follows
years.p: Teresa Nervosa quits the Butthole Surfers for good. Soon after she is diagnosed with an aneurysm, has brain surgery and begins suffering seizures set off by strobe lights.
years.xp: After the Widowermaker EP, their last Touch and Go release, the band left for Rough Trade. Kathleen Lynch stopped dancing with them the same year, and the shows became more predictable.

eras.title: Capitol, Pepper, and a lawsuit
eras.text: The band that once couldn't get its name in a newspaper signed to the Beatles' old label and scored a No. 1 modern rock hit. Then they sued Touch and Go over a handshake deal, and the indie world took sides.

years.h: Piouhgd, Rough Trade, and the first Lollapalooza
years.p: Piouhgd, pronounced "pissed off," disappoints critics, and Haynes and Leary later disowned it. The band still gets a slot on the first Lollapalooza that summer, and Rough Trade goes bankrupt.

years.h: Kurt Cobain meets Courtney Love at a Butthole Surfers show
years.p: Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love meet at a Butthole Surfers and [[L7|57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1]] concert, according to Wikipedia.

q: A lot of people gave us grief for doing that.
years.h: Independent Worm Saloon, produced by John Paul Jones · Capitol
years.p: Signed to Capitol in 1992, the band works with Led Zeppelin's [[John Paul Jones|4490113a-3880-4f5b-a39b-105bfceaed04]]. Who Was in My Room Last Night? is their first radio hit.
years.xp: Leary said in 2017 that being on the Beatles' and Dean Martin's label felt too weird to turn down. Wikipedia says the single reached No. 24 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart and the album No. 124 on the Billboard 200.
play: Who Was in My Room Last Night?

years.h: Gibby Haynes onstage at the Viper Room the night River Phoenix dies
years.p: Gibby Haynes is playing the Los Angeles club with P, his band with Johnny Depp, the night actor River Phoenix dies of a drug overdose there.
years.xp: Wikipedia, drawing on Leary and industry insiders, says Haynes was increasingly dependent on hard drugs in this period; Haynes downplayed their concern. P released one album on Capitol in 1995.

years.h: Jeff Pinkus leaves the Butthole Surfers
years.p: Bassist Jeff Pinkus quits after eight years. Haynes, Leary and Coffey carry on with fill-ins; Leary builds a producing career and Coffey runs his label, Trance Syndicate.

years.big: A handshake deal goes to federal court
q: We were outselling their entire catalog combined.
years.h: Butthole Surfers sue Touch and Go over a handshake deal
years.p: The band had no contract with Touch and Go, just a 50–50 split. When Corey Rusk won't improve their royalties or return their masters, they sue.
years.xp:
A district court sided with the band in 1998 and the Seventh Circuit affirmed in March 1999. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] was among the peers who criticized the band for suing; Haynes answered that Rusk sent accounting statements nobody could understand.

The band reissued their Touch and Go albums on Latino Buggerveil, and Touch and Go started asking bands to sign a memorandum of intent instead of shaking hands.

years.h: Electriclarryland and Pepper, a No. 1 hit
years.p: Pepper tops Billboard's Modern Rock chart and the album reaches No. 31 on the Billboard 200. Butthole Surfers songs land in Romeo + Juliet and Beavis and Butt-Head Do America.

years.h: Capitol shelves After the Astronaut
years.p: The follow-up to Electriclarryland is scrapped as the Butthole Surfers' relationship with Capitol sours, and they split bitterly with manager Tom Bunch.

eras.title: Weird Revolution and one more lap
eras.text: Free of Capitol, the band remade its shelved album for Hollywood Records, then went quiet. In 2008 the classic line-up, Teresa Nervosa included, came back for two years of touring.

years.h: Weird Revolution, the shelved album remade · Hollywood/Surfdog
years.p: Most of the After the Astronaut songs, re-recorded and pushed toward electronics and hip-hop. The Shame of Life reaches No. 24 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.h: The 1986–89 Butthole Surfers reunite
years.p: Jeff Pinkus and Teresa Nervosa rejoin for a tour of the East Coast and Europe, the first shows by that line-up since 1989. An appearance at All Tomorrow's Parties ends in a dispute with ATP founder Barry Hogan.

years.h: Gibby Haynes calls the Austin Halloween show maybe the last
years.p: At the last scheduled North American date of the reunion, Gibby Haynes tells the crowd the band played its first show as the Butthole Surfers in Austin, and this may be its last.

eras.title: The hole truth
eras.text: The band stopped touring and the story kept growing: a book, a death, a documentary, a Stranger Things sync and, twenty-eight years late, the album Capitol shelved.

years.h: Paul Leary says he's done touring
years.p: With the band on hiatus, Paul Leary says he no longer wants to play live: the hour onstage is fun, the other 23 hours are not.

years.h: What Does Regret Mean?, a Butthole Surfers visual history
years.p: Aaron Tanner's coffee-table book collects the band's flyers, photos and art.

years.h: Teresa Taylor dies at 60
years.p: Teresa Taylor dies of lung disease, which she had made public in 2021. The band posts that she passed away peacefully. Rolling Stone notes her 1991 cameo in Richard Linklater's Slacker put her on the film's poster.

years.h: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt premieres at SXSW
years.p: Tom Stern's Butthole Surfers documentary premieres at the Paramount Theatre in Austin during South by Southwest.

years.h: Butthole Surfers play the Egyptian Theatre in Los Angeles
years.p: After the documentary's West Coast premiere, Haynes, Leary, Coffey and Pinkus play a short set, their first as the Butthole Surfers since October 2017.

years.h: Human Cannonball turns up in Stranger Things
years.p: The Locust Abortion Technician song plays in Chapter 7 of the show's fifth season.

years.h: After the Astronaut, 28 years after Capitol shelved it
years.p: Announced March 17 with the single Jet Fighter, the album the Butthole Surfers made after Electriclarryland is set for release on Sunset Blvd Records.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Teresa Taylor dead at 60
